title: The dispensed prescription label exemption in 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(2), and dispensing without a prescription deemed misbranding
subtopic: Federal treatment of the dispensed prescription label
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(1) a prescription drug shall be dispensed only upon a written prescription of a practitioner licensed by law to administer the drug, upon an oral prescription of such practitioner reduced promptly to writing and filed by the pharmacist, or by refilling such a prescription if the refilling is authorized by the prescriber, and the act of dispensing a drug contrary to that paragraph shall be deemed to be an act which results in the drug being misbranded while held for sale. Under 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(2), any drug dispensed by filling or refilling a written or oral prescription of a practitioner licensed by law to administer it is exempt from the requirements of section 352, except paragraphs (a), (i)(2) and (3), (k), and (l), and the packaging requirements of paragraphs (g), (h), and (p), if the drug bears a label containing the name and address of the dispenser, the serial number and date of the prescription or of its filling, the name of the prescriber, and, if stated in the prescription, the name of the patient, and the directions for use and cautionary statements, if any, contained in the prescription; the exemption does not apply to a drug dispensed in the course of the conduct of a business of dispensing drugs pursuant to diagnosis by mail, or to a drug dispensed in violation of paragraph (1). Under 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(4)(A) a prescription drug is deemed misbranded if at any time prior to dispensing its label fails to bear, at a minimum, the symbol Rx only.
exam_relevance: Tests which misbranding provisions still bind a dispensed prescription, what its label must carry for the exemption to apply, and why dispensing without a valid prescription is itself misbranding.

authority.name: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

exceptions: The exemption does not apply to a drug dispensed in the course of the conduct of a business of dispensing drugs pursuant to diagnosis by mail, or to a drug dispensed in violation of 353(b)(1).
common_confusions: The exemption never lifts 352(a): a dispensed prescription whose labeling is false or misleading in any particular is still misbranded.
The imitation and offered-under-another-name grounds in 352(i)(2) and (3) and the packaging requirements of 352(g), (h) and (p) also survive the exemption.
Paragraphs (k) and (l) of 352, which 353(b)(2) still names, have been repealed.
The patient's name is a federal label element only if stated in the prescription; Massachusetts label requirements are a separate matter.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in 21 U.S.C. 352 and 353 on the Office of the Law Revision Counsel's United States Code site.
